`hookState.unchecked` isn't consulted. The agent is unchecked *because* its file can't be read — the one situation where "not installed" is unknowable — and we assert it anyway. Worse, we return before `removeAgentHooks`, so the built-in's `UninstallHooks` (which now errors loudly thanks to the fix) never even runs.

**Gap 2 — the closing message:** only `failedExternal`/`uncheckedPlugins` demote "uninstalled successfully". A built-in `UninstallHooks` failure lands in `agentHooksErr` → a stderr warning → then stdout still says "successfully", exit 0. The comment's rationale ("a built-in failure never fails: re-running reaches it") is broken by gap 1: the re-run early-returns "not installed", so re-running does *not* reach it.

Note gap 3 from the finding (unchecked built-ins invisible in the closing message) collapses into gap 2 now: an unreadable file makes the built-in unchecked *and* makes its `UninstallHooks` fail with the same read error — that's why the agent-level fix was the prerequisite.

**How I'd address it:**

1. **Early return:** add `&& len(hookState.unchecked) == 0`. When only unchecked agents remain, fall through — the confirmation already has the honest line for it ("Agent hooks that could not be checked (…)"), and the removal loop calls built-ins unconditionally, so the user gets `Warning: … read .claude/settings.json: permission denied` — path and cause, actionable. 2. **Closing message:** have `removeAgentHooks` also return the failed *built-in* names (it already separates them internally — today it keeps `failedExternal` and drops the built-in identity into the joined error). Then:

```go

    fmt.Fprintln(w, "\nEntire CLI uninstalled, but some agent hooks may remain - see the warnings above.")
```

"May remain" is the accurate word for built-ins too — an unreadable file proves we couldn't verify, not that hooks are inside.

3. **Exit code — the real judgment call:** whether `failedBuiltin` fails the command. I'd keep it strict-gated, same as external: the *message* stops lying unconditionally, the exit code stays 0 unless `--strict`. Rationale: consistency, and once gap 1 is fixed the "re-run reaches it" claim becomes true again — the re-run won't say "not installed", it'll re-attempt and re-warn. Yes — two real concerns, one of them the reason the gate exists.

**1. `Always` executes third-party binaries the user never authorized — on every uninstall, in every repo.**

Discovery isn't a read: it *executes* every `entire-agent-*` binary on `$PATH` (an `info` subprocess per binary), then the sweep executes each again (`are-hooks-installed`), and the removal can execute a *mutating* `uninstall-hooks`. The gate (`external_agents=true`) is the user's recorded authorization for Entire to run their plugins — set by `entire agent add` / `enable --agent`, i.e. an explicit choice. With `Always`, a user who never enabled any plugin runs `entire disable --uninstall` and Entire executes arbitrary binaries that merely match a name pattern on `$PATH`. `DiscoverAndRegisterAlways`'s own doc restricts it to "interactive setup flows where the user explicitly chooses agents" — a `--force` uninstall is the opposite of that.

Note the asymmetry you'd be trading: today's failure mode costs the user *one printed command* (the recovery line names `entire-agent-<name> uninstall-hooks` with the right env, at the exact moment it's still known). `Always`'s failure mode is unauthorized code execution as a default behavior. Those aren't comparable blast radii.

**2. It interacts badly with your own strict early-return.**

Under `--strict`, any unchecked agent now blocks "not installed". With `Always`, a crashed or junk-printing `entire-agent-*` binary on `$PATH` — completely unrelated to this repo — makes `entire disable --uninstall --strict` proceed and exit nonzero in a repo where Entire was *never installed*. With the gate, that can only happen in repos that actually enabled plugins.

Also mechanical: `TestRunUninstall_SkipsUnenabledExternalAgent` pins the gated behavior deliberately (its comment is exactly about not running write commands "against plugins the user never enabled").

**The idempotency problem is real though — and there's a fix without the regression:**

The non-idempotency comes from *ordering*: step 4 deletes `.entire/` (and with it the gate) even when external hook removal just failed. Instead of widening discovery, narrow the deletion: when an external agent's removal failed or couldn't be checked, **skip removing `.entire/`** (or at least report and keep it), so the gate survives and a re-run genuinely reaches the plugin. The steps model makes this cheap — `removeAgentHooks` already knows `externalProblem` before step 4 runs. The uninstall already exits nonzero-or-demoted in that case, so "uninstall left `.entire/` behind on purpose; fix the plugin and re-run" is a coherent story, and the "re-running will not reach these plugins" note becomes unnecessary — replaced by a true "re-run to finish".

My recommendation: keep `DiscoverAndRegister` gated; if the half-uninstall bothers you, make `.entire/` removal conditional on no external problems. Want me to implement that?

Make each uninstall step its own expert, and the whole command re-runnable

Every removal step — agent hooks, git hooks, session states, .entire/,
shadow branches — is now one function that prints its own report (removals
and nothing-to-remove lines to stdout, warnings with remedies to stderr),
handles its own errors with strict policy folded in, and returns a single
success boolean. runUninstall just chains the verdicts and prints the
closing line: any step failing exits nonzero, except external plugin
problems without --strict, which warn with a run-by-hand recovery command
and still close with success — Entire's own uninstall did complete, and
third-party code does not get to fail it unless asked. The removalStep
gathering machinery this replaces is gone.

Uninstall discovery switches to DiscoverAndRegisterAlways. The
external_agents setting that gated discovery lives in .entire/, which this
very command deletes, so a gated re-run after a partial uninstall could
never see the plugin whose hooks were left behind — the uninstall was
unrepeatable exactly when repeating it mattered. Ungated discovery keeps
every step isolated (.entire/ removal no longer depends on how the agent
step went) at the accepted, documented cost of executing entire-agent-*
binaries on $PATH even in repos that never enabled them.

Each step now always prints one line — what it removed or that there was
nothing to do — so the output shows what the uninstall actually did versus
what was already gone.

Tests pin the full exit-code policy table (strict/non-strict × external/
own-step), the own-step failure row via an unremovable .entire/, and the
convergence story: a run with three simultaneously failing steps exits
nonzero with each warning printed, and once the causes are fixed a re-run
removes exactly what survived and reports success.
